<reason>A won a close, high-quality clash by treating the motion as a fight over civic last word on narratives, not a facts-vs-meaning split. B’s best live route—checkable archives, child harm before elections, mixed-panel design—was repeatedly narrowed by A’s selection argument (first sentence, page, heading). B’s own “remove only for fraud, never for a verdict on empire” answer confirmed A’s transfer-of-power claim. B stayed eloquent and never collapsed, but adapted less well once the textbook-as-single-spine point landed.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: converting B’s staggered-term/no-firing-for-empire design into proof that insulation is ceremony for voters and last word for specialists, while insisting a marked “dispute” still selects the record children meet.</best_rebuttal>
